solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finished article by one who reckons this is buyable without prescription

parts.note: something finished is over
the definite article is THE
a person who reckons up numbers is a counter

explanation.surface: Someone who tallies figures declares a finished product fit for sale without a doctor's note.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines sold freely across a pharmacy's sales desk need no doctor's prescription.

clue.text: Bright scarlet lice endlessly alighting on big cat

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece landing on another sits above it, so it comes first
without its end, so the last letter of the word for lice is dropped

parts.note: lice are vermin
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: Bright red lice keep landing on a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece 'alighting on' another lands on top of it, so the shortened vermin comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermilion is a vivid red pigment and colour, a brilliant scarlet shade.

clue.text: For which one needs right type of oven

definitions.text: For which one needs right type of oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven

explanation.surface: A cook asks what dish calls for the correct kind of oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is a hop-drying kiln, common in Kent; the whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting meat is cooking it in a hot oven, so the joint is what needs one.

clue.text: One answer is to leave Ireland at the end of the winter

indicators.note: the named letters depart from the Latin word for Ireland, so they are taken out

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the final letter of the word the is used

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the solution is to leave Ireland once winter is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to leave' removes I and A from HIBERNIA, leaving HIBERN; 'end of' gives E from 'the'. 'winter' at the end is a verb, not a season.
explanation.definitionFit: To winter is to spend the cold season somewhere, as animals that sleep through it do.

clue.text: Sails from Cuba with reluctance

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba
loth means reluctant, unwilling

explanation.surface: A boat reluctantly sets sail from Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sails' looks like a verb but is the noun: canvas is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailcloth is the canvas of a ship, and sailors call a vessel's sails her cloth.

clue.text: A type of painting that's rarely seen?

definitions.text: A type of painting that's rarely seen?

parts.words: A type of painting that's rarely seen?
parts.note: suggests an obscure artwork, but means a layer of paint that is covered over by the top coat

explanation.surface: An art critic mentions a little-known genre of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The first layer of paint is hidden beneath the finishing coat, so it is rarely visible.

clue.text: Implied Roman historian disregarded us

indicators.note: the word us is ignored, so its letters are taken away

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian

explanation.surface: A Roman historian is said to have ignored people like us.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood without being stated, so it is implied.

clue.text: Bit of rice is served with fish and a faggot

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A dish of fish and a meatball is served with some rice.
explanation.walkthrough: A FAGGOT is a British meatball of minced offal, much like a rissole.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are balls of minced meat, fried or baked, so a rissole is a kind of faggot.

clue.text: Greek character, priest, receiving Bachelor of Divinity

indicators.note: the priest takes in the degree, so it goes inside

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
BD is the degree abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Greek cleric receives a theology degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A scrap — first in arena — blood flows from it

parts.note: an ort is a scrap of leftover food

indicators.note: the opening letter of arena is taken

explanation.surface: A fight in an arena draws blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood out of the heart.

clue.text: Favours involving wharf in dull provincial place

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: boons are favours
a dock is a wharf

explanation.surface: Favours are traded on the wharf of a dreary country town.
explanation.definitionFit: The boondocks is slang for remote backwoods country, a dull rural backwater.

clue.text: British surgeon exposes lump on skin

parts.note: Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who pioneered antiseptics

explanation.surface: A British doctor reveals a growth on a patient's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A blister is a raised bubble of fluid under the skin.

clue.text: Hornblower's short speech after end of skirmish

definitions.note: the definition is the possessive name; it stands for the first name of the fictional naval officer

indicators.note: the speech follows that letter
the final letter of skirmish is taken
cut short, so the last letter of the speech word is dropped

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A naval officer makes a brief address after a skirmish ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Hornblower is C S Forester's fictional Royal Navy captain; 'Hornblower's' means his given name.
explanation.definitionFit: C S Forester's naval hero is named Horatio Hornblower, so it is his first name.

clue.text: Bail dislodged? One makes an excuse

indicators.note: knocked out of place, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: In cricket the bails are knocked off, and a batter finds an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: BAILS are the small wooden pieces resting on top of cricket stumps; 'dislodged' is the rearranging signal, and 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea of being elsewhere, and loosely any excuse.

clue.text: Mario, not a fickle lover

indicators.note: changeable, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Mario is described as not a fickle lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover or sweetheart, from Italian.

clue.text: Where boats may be moored in Alaskan port

definitions.meaning: a place where vessels drop anchor
the largest city of Alaska, a port on Cook Inlet

explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a mooring place, and Anchorage is Alaska's chief port city.

clue.text: Bird coming from rock, crane that's injured

indicators.note: hurt and so damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird emerges from behind a rock as a wounded crane.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a secretive bird of the rail family living in fields.

clue.text: Girl runs across friend from her former college?

indicators.note: the runs cross over the friend and land beyond it, after it

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name
a mate is a friend
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A girl dashes over to a friend she knew at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' moves R past MATE so it ends up last. The question mark admits that the answer is anyone's old college, not just a woman's.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or university one attended.

clue.text: Listen and learn, dean ordered

indicators.note: put in order differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dean orders students to listen and learn.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom meaning to pay attention, to hear someone out.

clue.text: Hide the real fake

indicators.note: not genuine, so the letters are a false arrangement

explanation.surface: Is this hide real or fake?
explanation.definitionFit: Hide is the skin of an animal, which tanned becomes leather.

clue.text: Scheduled to resign upon return

indicators.note: on coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to demit is to resign an office

explanation.surface: Someone is scheduled to resign on getting back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timed has been arranged for a set moment, as scheduled.

clue.text: Helping pretty girl with work

parts.note: doll is slang for a pretty girl
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A pretty girl helps out with the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a large spoonful, a serving or helping of food.

clue.text: Run off with sailor back out east

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the east letter is taken out

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: A man runs off with a sailor heading back east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is a verb, SECOND, and 'out' drops its E to leave SCOND; it is not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to flee secretly, to run away from duty or the law.

clue.text: Pretentiousness shown at society parties

parts.note: side is dated slang for swagger or pretentiousness, as in putting on side

explanation.surface: Airs and graces are on display at society parties.
explanation.definitionFit: In a contest or dispute the opposing parties are the two sides.

clue.text: Greyhound, say, to disappear out of sight

parts.note: a greyhound is an example of a dog
to go is to vanish, disappear

explanation.surface: A greyhound races out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: To lie DOGGO is British slang for keeping hidden and still.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggo is slang for in hiding, as when someone lies low unseen.

clue.text: Girl eating a chewy sweet

indicators.note: the girl takes the letter inside

parts.note: Carmel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl munches a chewy sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a toffee-like sweet made of boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Went on horseback to ring to see competition in cowboy skills

parts.note: rode is the past of ride
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A rider goes to the ring to watch a cowboy contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show where cowboys compete at riding broncos and roping cattle.

clue.text: Flowering plant in garden, possibly among new-mown hay

indicators.note: the scrambled garden goes amid the other letters
freshly cut, so the letters are rearranged
maybe in another order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flowering plant grows in a garden among freshly cut hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles 'garden' and 'new-mown' scrambles 'hay'; 'among' sets the first result between the second's last two letters. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are shrubs bearing large rounded heads of blue, pink or white flowers.

clue.text: One teetotaller in party gets the same again

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party
one is the Roman numeral I
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, a teetotaller

explanation.surface: A non-drinker at a party orders the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the aforesaid repeated, used to avoid saying the same again.

clue.text: Stop rowing and relax

definitions.meaning: literally, to pause pulling the oars
to take a break after effort

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to ease off after effort, from rowers pausing with blades lifted.
